creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 13, item 3.

```rad
count = 10
items = []
fn plain_assign():
    count = count + 1
fn plus_assign():
    count += 5
    items += ["x"]

plain_assign()
print(count)          // 10
plus_assign()
print(count, items)   // 15 [ "x" ]
```

Reproduces on main, and `rad check` is clean. The two forms read as the same statement, so the choice silently decides whether shared state changes.

This is not the bug sprint `a_25NhxlPan` fixed (a function with a local of the same name). Here the function has no local; `+=` finds the global, plain `=` declares a local. Either both forms follow one rule, or the checker warns when a function assigns a global's name; either way reference/syntax's Scoping section should state the rule.

Where: `rts/converter.go` `convertCompoundAssign` sets `UpdateEnclosing`; plain assignment does not.
title: Inside a function, x += v writes the global while x = x + v creates a local
